# thoth_evidence_pack (Resource)

Builds a signed evidence pack for a period. Destroying it removes it from state only; the pack stays in Thoth. Download and verify packs with thothctl.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "thoth_evidence_pack" "september" {
  period_start = "2026-09-01T00:00:00Z"
  period_end   = "2026-10-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

Then download and verify it offline with `thothctl evidence pack download --pack-id <id>` and
`thothctl evidence verify --pack <parts>`.

## How it behaves

- Leave out both `period_start` and `period_end` for the previous calendar month. A period covers
  at most 31 days and must already have ended.
- A workspace builds one pack at a time. If a pack for the same period is already queued or
  building, this resource adopts it; for another period, apply fails until that build finishes.
- `wait_for_ready` (default true) waits up to `wait_timeout_minutes` (default 30). A failed build
  is an error. If the wait times out, the pack is kept in state and keeps building; the next
  refresh records the result.
- A pack is evidence, not configuration. Change `trigger` or the period to build another.
  Destroying the resource only removes it from state; the pack stays in Thoth.
- Part locations are never in state. Download needs a paid plan, or a trial within its read-only
  retention window.

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `period_end` (String) RFC 3339 end of the period, exclusive: at most 31 days after the start, and already passed.
- `period_start` (String) RFC 3339 start of the period, with period_end. Default: the previous calendar month.
- `trigger` (String) Change this value to build another pack.
- `wait_for_ready` (Boolean) Wait until the pack is ready or failed (default true). A failed build is an error.
- `wait_timeout_minutes` (Number) How long to wait (1-120, default 30).

### Read-Only

- `completed_at` (String) When the build finished.
- `created_at` (String) When the pack was queued.
- `error` (String) Why a build failed.
- `id` (String) Pack ID.
- `part_count` (Number) Number of signed parts in a ready pack.
- `status` (String) queued, building, ready or failed.
- `totals_json` (String) What the pack holds (attestations, chain events, parts) as JSON.

## Import

```shell
terraform import thoth_evidence_pack.september <pack_id>
```
